texts.preamble: Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 1 Scch - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 Kabc020019792024 In The Court Of The Ix Addl. Small Causes And, Acjm, (Scch-7), Bengaluru. Before: Sri. Shyam Prakash B.A.L, Llb., Ix Addl. Small Causes Judge, Court of Small Causes, Member, Mact-7, Bengaluru. Dated this 28th day of March 2025 Mvc. No.2614 C/w 2615 of 2023 Petitioner
texts.facts: . 3 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 2. The Petitioner in MVC No.2614/2023 has filed petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/-for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16-03-2023. 3. The Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 has filed petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1989, seeking compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-for the injures sustained by him in the road traffic accident occurred on 16-03-2023. 4 It is the case of the petitioners in both cases that, on 16- 03-2023 at about 8.40 a.m., within the jurisdiction of R.R. Nagara Traffic Police Station, at G.K. Ground Signal, when the Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 2 riding the unoffending Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-09-JG-5792 along with Petitioner in MVC No.2614/2023 as a pillion rider drove the same from Sheshadri Iyer Road - RMC circle towards Gayathribhavan and stopped at the G K Ground Junction (Puttagopalakrishna shetty circle) and after getting green signal when the rider of the unoffending 4 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 vehicle drove the same, at that time the driver/ accused driving the offending KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42-F-1974 drove the same from Irvin Road Rawilway station towards A.V. Circle by ignoring the signal and jumped the red signal in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the said unoffending vehicle as a result the rider/Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 sustained grievous injuries to his right hand, right leg and other parts of the body and the Petitioner in MVC No.2614/2023 sustained simple injuries to face, right hand, right leg and other parts of the body. Therefore informant/ Chinnaswamigowda lodged complaint before the R.R. Nagara Traffic Police station. Accordingly, a case was registered in their Crime No.18/2023 and prepared F.I.R. for the offence punishable under sections 279, 337 and 338 of IPC R/w Section 119, 177 of MV Act and submitted to the jurisdictional judicial Magistrate and the superior officers and investigation was taken up by the Investigating Officer. 5. After the accident the Petitioner in MVC.2614/2023 was shifted to JSS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has 5 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 spent more than Rs.1,00,000/- medical, conveyance, nourishment and other charges expenditure. 6. After the accident the Petitioner in MVC.2615/2023 was shifted to JSS Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and undergone surgery therein and he has spent more than Rs.5,00,000/- medical, conveyance, nourishment and other charges expenditure. 7. Further it is alleged that prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner in MVC.2614/2023 was hale, healthy and he was aged about 17 years and he was doing agriculture Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 3 and coolie work and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m.. Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the Petitioner has became permanently disabled and he is unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident. 8. Further it is alleged that prior to the alleged accident the Petitioner in MVC.2615/2023 was hale, healthy and he was aged about 25 years and he was doing street food vendor work and earning an income of Rs.30,000/- p.m. Due to the injuries sustained in the alleged accident the Petitioner has became permanently disabled and he is 6 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 unable to do his work normally as he was doing prior to the occurrence of the alleged accident. 9. The alleged accident is occurred due to fault and negligence act of the driver of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42-F-1974. Respondent is the RC owner of the said offending vehicle, as such the respondent is liable to pay compensation to Petitioners in both case. Hence Petitioners filed the respective present claim petitions for seeking compensation. 10. In response to the notice, the respondent has appeared through their counsel and filed their written statement in both clubbed cases. 11. In the written statement of the Respondent, it has admitting the ownership of the offending KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42-F-1974 and by denying the petition averments in part and contended that, this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the said offending KSRTC bus, as such they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners. Further denied the age, income and occupation of the Petitioners and expenses incurred towards medication and other charges. Further 7 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 respondent contended that, the compensation claimed by the Petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and imaginary. Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent prayed for dismissal of claim petitions. On the basis of above pleadings following Issues were framed. 13. In order to prove the case of Petitioners, the Petitioners in MVC No.2614/2023 got examined as PW-1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.14 documents. The Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 got examined himself as PW-2 and got marked Ex.P-15 to P.20 documents. 5 Record Technician of J.S.S. Hospital got examined as PW-5 and PW-6 and got marked and Ex.P.25 to Ex.P.32 documents and closed their side. The driver of the KSRTC Bus got examined as RW-1 and closed their side. 16. Issue No.1 in both cases:- These petitions are filed U/sec.166 of M.V.Act 1989 for seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by the Petitioners in both cases respectively due to alleged accident. 17. The Petitioners in both case contended that, on 16-03- 2023 at about 8.40 a.m., within the jurisdiction of R.R. Nagara Traffic Police Station, at G.K. Ground Signal, when the Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 riding the unoffending Honda Activa Scooter bearing registration No.KA-09-JG-5792 along with Petitioner in MVC No.2614/2023 as a pillion rider drove the same from Sheshadri Iyer Road - RMC circle towards Gayathribhavan and stopped at the G K Ground Junction (Puttagopalakrishna shetty circle) and after getting green signal when the rider of the unoffending vehicle drove the same, at that time the driver/ accused driving the offending KSRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42-F-1974 drove the same from Irvin Road Rawilway station towards A.V. Circle by ignoring the 10 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 signal and jumped the red signal in a high speed, rash and negligent manner so as to endangering human life and dashed against the said unoffending vehicle as a result the rider/Petitioner in MVC No.2615/2023 Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 6 sustained grievous injuries to his right hand, right leg and other parts of the body and the Petitioner in MVC No.2614/2023 sustained simple injuries to face, right hand, right leg and other parts of the body.
texts.arguments: It is contended that the alleged accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle. The Respondent has admitted that it is the owner of the offending vehicle and his version is that this accident occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and there is no negligence on the part of the driver of the said offending KSRTC bus, as such they are not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioners. Further denied the age, income and occupation of the Petitioners and expenses incurred towards medication and other charges. Further respondent contended that, the compensation claimed by the Petitioners is highly excessive, exorbitant and imaginary. Hence, on all these grounds, the respondent prayed for dismissal of claim petitions. Further he has denied that he has not sustained grievous injuries in the alleged accident. Further he has denied that he has not taken treatment at Shivarathri Shiva Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 8 Hospital as inpatient. Further he has denied that he has not produced any documents to show that he has taken follow-up treatment. Further he has denied that he has not incurred such expenses towards transportation. Further he has denied that he has not incurred Rs.5,00,000/- towards his medical expenditure. Further he has deposed that he is working under Murthy and earning salary of Rs.30,000/- p.m. and in that regard he has not produced documents. He is not an owner of the Gobi Manchuri Shop. He has denied that he is not working under Murthy in that Gobi Manchuri Shop and earning salary of Rs.30,000/- p.m. Further he has denied that he is hale and healthy and he is not suffering from pain and difficulties and he is doing his work and other regular activities as past. Further he has denied that the alleged accident occurred due to negligence and fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the driver of the offending vehicle. Further he denied that in order to get more compensation in collusion with the police they have falsely implicated the accused in this case and produced concocted and created documents and he has filed the false evidence affidavit and deposing falsely. 28. Admittedly, the accused is the driver of the offending vehicle and further admitted that, Petitioners in both cases have sustained injuries due to alleged accident 19 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 11 caused by the offending vehicle in question. The counsel for Respondent claimed the said Accused to be innocent and further the counsel for Respondent contended that, the alleged accident occurred due to fault of the rider of the unoffending vehicle and no fault of the accused, slowly he may be driving and therefore he cannot be held to be negligent and further contended that the police have falsely implicated the accused in this case and filed false Charge Sheet against the accused and therefore the Charge Sheet is not conclusive proof and the Petitioner has established his case by preponderance of evidence that there was no negligence on the part of the injured and they were not responsible for the accident. Proof of rashness and negligence on the part of the driver of the vehicle, is therefore, sing qua non for maintining an application under Section 166 of the MV Act. But simply the involvement of the Bus in the accident cannot make the Respondent liable to pay compensation unless it can be held on the basis of material on record that the accident was caused by rash and negligent act of the driver and it is well settle law that the tribinal is not bound by the decision recorded in a criminal case as this is an indepentnt proceedings and in this regard the counsel produced bundles of decisions, viz., (2005) 6 SCC 172, (2007) 13 SCC 476, 20 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 (2014) SCC 254, order dated 03.01.2011 in MFA No.2829/2009, order dated 09.02.2016 in MFA No.2921/2012, ILR 2009 KAR 3562, (2011) 2 KantLJ 614 and ILR 2003 KAR 409. 29. The Learned counsel for the Petitioner has contended that the injured Petitioner was aged about 17 years at the time of Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 13 accident and he is doing agriculture & coolie work and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m., and the Petitioner has incurred expenses towards medical expenditure. As such the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the head of pain and suffering, mental agony, medical expenses, special diet, conveyance, loss of future income due to disability, loss of amenities and loss of income during laid up period and prays to award the compensation as prayed in the petition. 23 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 31. On the other hand the learned counsel for Respondent contended that even though the Petitioner claimed that his earning was about Rs.20,000/- p.m., the same is not established by the claimant by producing the documents. Since the Petitioner has not established his income, he is not entitled for compensation towards such prospects and hence prays dismissal of the petition. 32. The petitioner contended that as on the date of the accident he was aged about 17 years at the time of accident and he relied on the Ex.P.13/Adhar Card of the Petitioner and wherein the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 01.01.2006 and this accident was took place on 16.03.2023. Hence it is clear that on the strength of the Ex.P-13/Adhar Card as on the date of the accident the Petitioner was aged about 17 years 2 months. Hence the age of the Petitioner is considered as 17 years and he is a minor as on the date of the accident. 33. It is not in dispute that the Petitioner sustained injuries in the alleged road traffic accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver/accused. In the instance case the petitioner claimed that he was doing agriculture and coolie work 24 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 and earning an income of Rs.20,000/- p.m. But he has not produced any documents to prove the income of the Petitioner from the alleged work. 34. In the chief examination of PW-3/Dr.Nagaraj.B.N, Orthopedics Surgeon deposed that in the alleged road traffic accident the petitioner has sustained degloving Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 14 injury over the right elbow and the Petitioner taken treatment at JSS Hospital with wound debridement and skin grafting and later discharged and on 31.07.2023 with contracture of the right arm and underwent contracture release with minor skin grafting. Further deposed that the Petitioner now complains of weakness in the right elbow, unable to lift heavy objects in the right hand, unable to fold to extent the right hand and on examination the Petitioner has unhealthy scar over the right elbow proximally into the lower third arm and distally into the proximal forearm with restricted right elbow movements and recent X-ray shows evidence of ossification over the elbow and the Petitioner has sustained disability of the right arm at 39% and whole body physical disability at 13%. Further he has denied that the Petitioner is hale and healthy and he is not suffering from pain or difficulties. Further he has denied that there will be no disability for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner. Further he has denied that the Petitioner has no difficulties in the movement of his right ankle. Further he has denied that as he has not treated doctor he is not right person to assess the disability of the Petitioner. Further he has denied that in order to help the petitioner he has assessed disability on the higher side and filed false affidavit and deposing falsely. 35. As the occupation of the petitioner is considered as agriculture coolie work, while doing agriculture work the petitioner has to stand and sit for long time, he has to bend, put weight on both hands and legs, he has to use hands and legs and he has to sit down, climbing upstairs and walk while doing the work. But due to the injuries sustained in this accident the petitioner has not in position to do the said work as past. The doctor has assessed the total disability of the right arm at 39% and whole body physical disability at 13%. Hence by 26 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 Basavaraju C vs K.S.R.T.C on 28 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56075969/ 15 considering the age, occupation, nature of injury and the functional disability of the petitioner is considered as 13% to the whole body. As the petitioner is a minor and he is doing agriculture and coolie work due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is having difficulty to lift heavy objects in the right hand, unable to fold, to extant the right hand fully, weakness in the right elbow, unable to lift due to which in his future life the petitioner may suffer from disability. 36. The alleged accident is occurred in the year 2023, in this regard in the authority reported in order dated 27.09.2024 in MFA No.426/2020 C/w MFA No.4124/2020 C/w MFA No.7008/2021 in the case of Master Karthik.R.., V/s National Insurance Company Ltd., and Others of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru., wherein it is held that in case of a non- earning member, i.e., minor if disability is 10% upto 30% to the whole body is Rs.5,01,521/- for the year 2023. In this case on hand the doctor has assessed the disability of the right arm at 39% and whole body physical disability at 13%. In this case as per the evidence of doctor the petitioner is having permanent physical disability to an extent of 13% to the whole body as such by relying on the above said authority I am of 27 SCCH - 7 M.V.C.No.2614 & 2615 of 2023 the considered view that the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,01,521/- under the head of pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience, and discomforts etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of permanent disability. 37. Further due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner was admitted in the hospital. Hence during this period his parents have attended the hospital and they have lost some earnings due to the hospitalization of the petitioner for the injuries sustained in the accident. Hence an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- is awarded under the head of discomfort, inconvenience and loss of earnings to the parents during the period of hospitalization. 38. Further the Petitioner has produced hospital and medical expenses as per Ex.P.9 for an amount of Rs.86,366/-. Hence the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.86,366/- under the head of hospital and medical expenses. The alleged accident is occurred in the year 2023, in this regard in the authority reported in order dated 27.09.2024 in MFA No.426/2020 C/w MFA No.4124/2020 C/w MFA No.7008/2021 in the case of Master Karthik.R.., V/s National Insurance Company Ltd., and Others of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru., wherein it is held that in case of a non- earning member, i.e., minor if disability is 10% upto 30% to the whole body is Rs.5,01,521/- for the year 2023.
